chapter.title: Getting in and standing up

cards.body: Think of the pool as a bed you lie on, not a floor you fall through, and tonight's one skill is **getting out of that bed**: from lying forward in the water to standing on your feet in under 2 seconds. Picture someone sitting up in bed in the morning: knees come in, hands push down on the mattress, feet find the floor. That's the whole move.
cards.simpler: Think of the pool as a bed you lie on, not a floor you fall through. Tonight you learn one thing: **getting out of that bed**. You go from lying forward in the water to standing on your feet in under 2 seconds. Picture sitting up in bed in the morning. Knees come in, hands push down on the mattress, feet find the floor. That is the whole move.

cards.prompt: You're lying face down in chest-deep water. The pool floor is right there under you. You want to stand. What do you do first?

options.text: Pull your knees in towards your chest
Lift your head high and reach for the wall
Kick hard and swim for the shallow steps

whyNot.b: That's the reach, not the stand: lifting your head alone tips your legs down slowly, and your hands aren't pushing yet, so you flail. Knees first.
whyNot.c: That's swimming, not standing: in chest-deep water the floor is already under you, so you don't need to go anywhere.

cards.reteach: Your legs are the only part of you that can reach the floor. If they're trailing out behind you, you can't stand. Tuck your knees under you first, like sitting up in bed, and your feet are suddenly right where the floor is.

cards.title: Getting in, and the three-part stand
cards.body:
Get in by the steps or ladder, facing the ladder, one hand on each rail. Walk in until the water is at the top of your chest, head and shoulders dry. This is *chest-deep*, and here the floor is always one movement away.

Walk across the pool. Push the water aside with your hands as you go. You'll feel it slow you down and hold you up a little at the same time. That small lift is the bed.

The stand-up has 3 parts, always in this order: **knees in** to your chest, hands press down flat towards the floor, feet plant and push up. Say it as you do it: knees, hands, feet.
cards.simpler: Get in by the steps or ladder. Face the ladder, one hand on each rail. Walk in until the water reaches the top of your chest. Your head and shoulders stay dry. This is chest-deep water, and here the floor is always one move away. Walk across the pool, pushing the water aside with your hands. It slows you a bit and lifts you a bit. That small lift is the bed. The stand-up has 3 parts, always in this order: **knees in** to your chest, hands press down flat, feet plant and push up. Say it as you go: knees, hands, feet.

cards.title: Dana, first lesson, chest-deep
cards.body: Dana, 34, is in chest-deep water. The instructor says lie forward, I've got your hands. Dana lies forward, face above the water, and her feet drift off the floor. Her brain announces that this is the end. The instructor says 'knees, hands, feet.' Dana pulls her knees in, presses her palms down, and is **standing before the sentence finishes**. She looks down. The water is at her chest. It was at her chest the whole time.
cards.simpler: Dana, 34, is in chest-deep water. The instructor says lie forward, I've got your hands. Dana lies forward, face above the water, and her feet drift off the floor. Her brain tells her this is the end. The instructor says 'knees, hands, feet.' Dana pulls her knees in, presses her palms down, and is **standing before the sentence finishes**. She looks down. The water is at her chest. It was at her chest the whole time.

cards.prompt: Omar is in chest-deep water holding the wall, feet off the floor, legs floating out behind him. He wants to stand without the wall. Which gets him up fastest?

options.text: Let go, keep his legs straight, lift his head and wait for his feet to sink
Pull his knees to his chest, let go, press his hands down, plant his feet
Grip the wall tighter and swing one leg down at a time

whyNot.a: That's waiting for the water to do it, not the stand-up: straight legs sink slowly, and you tip about while they do.
whyNot.c: That's a wall move, not the stand-up: it works, but only where there's a wall. The 3-part stand works anywhere you can reach the floor.

cards.reteach: Knees in makes you a ball, and a ball in water rolls upright on its own. Then your hands press the water down, which pushes your chest up, and your feet land. Three parts, two seconds, no wall needed.

cards.title: Why it works, and when to use it
cards.body:
Tucking your knees makes you a ball, and a ball in water rolls so your heavy hips and legs point down. You don't fight to get upright. You tuck, and the water does the turning.

Pressing your hands down does the rest. Water pushes back on anything you push, so flat palms pressed towards the floor lift your shoulders up. Then your feet find the floor and you stand.

Do this stand-up 10 times in a row tonight, from lying forward, until it's dull. **Dull is the goal.** Floating, gliding and swimming in later chapters all end with this exact move, so your body needs to do it without being asked.
cards.simpler: Tuck your knees and you become a ball. A ball in water rolls so the heavy end points down. Your hips and legs are the heavy end. So you tuck, and the water turns you upright for you. Pressing your hands down does the rest. Water pushes back on anything you push, so flat palms pressed down lift your shoulders. Then your feet find the floor. Do this stand-up 10 times in a row tonight until it feels dull. **Dull is the goal.** Floating, gliding and swimming all end with this move, so your body must do it without thinking.

cards.body: Priya feels her feet lift off the floor, panics, and does what land taught her: she throws her head and arms straight up. Her legs swing down late, water goes in her mouth, and she gasps. The tell is **arms going up**. In water, up comes from pushing down. If you see your hands above the surface, you've skipped the knees and the press.
cards.simpler: Priya feels her feet lift off the floor and panics. She does what land taught her: she throws her head and arms straight up. Her legs swing down late, water goes in her mouth, and she gasps. The warning sign is **arms going up**. In water, up comes from pushing down. If your hands are above the surface, you skipped the knees and the press.

cards.prompt: A friend asks what to do if they lie forward in the shallow end and feel like they're going under. Which answer is right?

options.text: Kick hard and keep your head up until you reach the wall
Knees in, hands press down, feet plant. Two seconds and you're standing
Take a big breath and hold still until someone helps

whyNot.a: That's the swim-for-safety instinct, not the stand: kicking stretches your legs out behind you, the opposite of tucking, and the floor was already under you.
whyNot.c: That's holding still, not standing: a big breath helps you float, but it won't put your feet on the floor. The tuck does that.

cards.reteach: In chest-deep water the floor is never more than one tuck away. Knees in turns you upright, hands pressing down lifts your chest, feet plant and you stand. Say it like a phone number: knees, hands, feet.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: In chest-deep water the floor is always one move away: **knees in, hands press down, feet plant**, and you're standing in under 2 seconds. Do it until it's dull, because every swimming skill after this one ends with it.
cards.simpler: In chest-deep water the floor is always one move away. **Knees in, hands press down, feet plant**, and you are standing in under 2 seconds. Do it until it feels dull. Every swimming skill after this one ends with this same move, so your body needs to know it by heart.

cards.body: Tonight, on your bed or the floor: lie face down, then do knees in, hands press down, feet plant, saying the words out loud. 10 times. Your body learns the order dry, so the pool only has to add the wet.
cards.simpler: Tonight, on your bed or the floor: lie face down. Then do knees in, hands press down, feet plant, saying the words out loud as you go. Do it 10 times. Your body learns the **order while dry**, so in the pool it only has to add the wet.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now get into chest-deep water, walk across it, and stand up from lying forward in under 2 seconds, every time.
